info.title: Matching & Merge API
info.description:
The Matching & Merge API provides duplicate detection, match verification, and manual merge/unmerge operations — the core value proposition of MDM.

**Matching** detects potential duplicates by evaluating configurable match rules against entity attributes. Match rules use tokenization (generating search tokens from attribute values) and comparison (scoring similarity between token pairs) to produce match candidates. Candidates above the auto-merge threshold are merged automatically; those in the suspect range are flagged for manual review.

**Merge** (`_sameAs`) combines two entity profiles into one golden record, consolidating all crosswalks and re-evaluating survivorship. **Unmerge** (`_unmerge`) reverses a merge by separating a contributor crosswalk back into its own entity.

The API also supports manual match/not-match marking, transitive match discovery, match explanation (verify), and bulk operations.

environment.description: Reltio environment name (e.g. dev, qa, prod)

get.description:
Retrieves potential matches (suspected duplicates) for a specific entity. Results are entities that the matching engine identified as likely duplicates based on configured match rules.

Use `forceMatch=true` to recalculate matches in real-time instead of using pre-computed results. Use `transitive=true` to include transitive matches (matches of matches).

200.description: Potential match results for the entity.

post.description:
Finds matches for one or more input entities against the existing entity population. Unlike `GET /{id}/_matches` which looks up pre-computed matches, this endpoint evaluates match rules in real-time against the provided entity data.

Useful for "what-if" scenarios — check if incoming data would match existing records before actually ingesting it.

200.description: Match results for each input entity.

post.description: Like `_matches` but includes match scores — numeric similarity values for each match rule that fired. Scores help rank matches by confidence and are essential for building match review UIs where data stewards need to see *how closely* two records match.

Explains *why* two entities match or don't match. Returns a detailed breakdown of which match rules were evaluated, which tokens were compared, and the resulting scores.

This is the primary debugging and explanation endpoint for the matching engine — essential for data stewards investigating match decisions and for developers tuning match rules.

Previews what would happen if a contributor were unmerged from a merged entity. Returns whether the unmerge is possible and which match rules would still connect the entities after separation.

Use this before calling `_unmerge` to understand the consequences — if match rules would immediately re-merge the entities, the unmerge may not be meaningful.

Low-level match candidate discovery. Returns the list of entity URIs that would be evaluated as potential matches for the input entity, grouped by match method.

Unlike `_matches` (which returns full match results with scores), this endpoint shows the *candidate pool* — the set of entities whose match tokens overlap with the input. Useful for diagnosing why matches are or aren't being found.

200.description: Match candidates grouped by match method.

post.description:
Manually merges two entities into one golden record. The entity specified by `{entityId}` is merged with the entity specified by the `uri` query parameter.

After merge, all crosswalks from both entities are consolidated into one profile, and survivorship rules are re-evaluated to determine the golden record attribute values. The losing entity's URI redirects to the winner.

Use `explicitWinner` to force which entity survives (by default, the platform decides based on data richness).

202.description: Merge accepted. Returns the merged entity.

404.description: One or both entities not found.

post.description:
Unmerges a contributor from a merged entity, splitting it back into two separate profiles. The `contributorURI` query parameter specifies which contributor crosswalk to separate.

After unmerge, the original entity retains all remaining crosswalks and re-evaluates survivorship. The extracted contributor becomes a new independent entity.

Returns both resulting entities as a pair.

get.description: Retrieves entities that have been explicitly marked as "not a match" for this entity. Not-match marks suppress future match suggestions between the pair.

post.description: Marks two entities as "not a match" — suppresses future match suggestions between them. A data steward decision that the matching engine should not propose this pair again.

delete.description: Removes a not-match mark between two entities, allowing the matching engine to suggest them as potential matches again.

get.description: Retrieves entities explicitly marked as matches for this entity (manual match confirmations).

200.description: List of confirmed match entity URIs.

post.description: Manually confirms two entities as a match. Unlike `_sameAs` (which merges immediately), this marks them for future merge processing.

delete.description: Removes a manual match confirmation between two entities.

get.description:
Retrieves transitive matches — entities that match entities that match the specified entity. If A matches B and B matches C, then C is a transitive match of A.

Use `deep` to control how many levels of transitivity to follow, and `showPath=true` to see the chain of matches that connects the entities.

post.description:
Marks multiple entity pairs as "not a match" in a single request. More efficient than individual `_notMatch` calls when processing batch stewardship decisions.

The request body contains a `pairs` array with `first`/`second` entity URIs. Use `failFast=true` to stop on the first error.

VerifyMatchRequest.title: Verify Match Request
VerifyMatchRequest.description: Request body for match explanation between two entities.

first.description: First entity (full EntityTO or URI reference).

second.description: Second entity (full EntityTO or URI reference).

matchGroups.description: Optional custom match groups to evaluate instead of the tenant's configured rules.

VerifyMatchesExplanation.title: Verify Matches Explanation
VerifyMatchesExplanation.description: Detailed match explanation showing which rules were evaluated and their results.

summary.description: Human-readable summary of the match result.

matchTokensSummary.description: Summary of match token overlaps between the two entities.

applicableMatchGroups.description: Which match groups apply to both entities.

candidatesDiscovery.description: How match candidates were discovered (token intersection details).

rules.description: Rule-by-rule breakdown. Keys are rule URIs, values contain comparator results and scores.

manualMatches.description: Any manual match/not-match marks between the pair.

rules.description: Match rules that would still connect the entities after unmerge.

entity.description: The entity to find candidates for (full EntityTO).

matchDocumentsEqual.description: Whether generated and stored match documents are identical.

byMatchMethods.description: Candidates grouped by match method URI.

UnmergePair.title: Unmerge Pair
UnmergePair.description: The two entities resulting from an unmerge operation.

a.description: The original entity with remaining crosswalks.

b.description: The newly separated entity from the unmerged contributor.

failFast.description: Stop processing on the first error.

pairs.description: Results for each pair, including any error codes.

errorCode.description: Error code if the operation failed for this pair.
